text: 🇲🇽✊ Minimum wage up 157%. Labor poverty at historic low. "The minimum wage increased more than 157%. Wages rose — poverty fell.

🇲🇽🌎 "We are not anyone's piñata. Everyone mind their own business." "Not everything happens in Mexico. 🇲🇽✊ "Twelve pieces of good news that show the strength of the Mexican economy." "Record FDI. 2.5% unemployment — among the three lowest in the world. 🇲🇽🏭 21 billion pesos in pharmaceutical investment announced today. "Plan México means Mexico produces more of what it needs — and exports to other countries." — Claudia Sheinbaum, announcing pharma sovereignty push 7 companies (Abbott, Bristol Myers Squibb, Sanofi, Bayer, Liomont, Neolpharma, Opella) committed 21B+ pesos. Local production of medicines, active ingredients, and insulin via technology transfer.

Joint ground operations are not allowed. That's what Mexican authorities are for." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on US-Mexico security cooperation Sheinbaum drew a firm line on bilateral operations. Collaboration yes — subordination no.

🇲🇽📊 SHEINBAUM FIRES BACK AT MOODY'S WITH 12 HARD FACTS — RECORD FDI, 2.5% UNEMPLOYMENT, PEMEX DEBT DOWN $20B

Sheinbaum responded to Moody's downgrade with 12 economic indicators: record FDI in Q1 2026 — the highest in Mexico's history. Unemployment at 2.5%, top 3 globally. Peso stable at 17.40. Gasoline prices among the world's lowest despite the Iran war driving global energy costs up.

Pemex cut its debt by $20 billion. The fiscal deficit dropped 1.5% of GDP. Tax collection rose from 14.7% to 15.2% of GDP. April registered the highest formal employment ever recorded.

"Twelve good news items, twelve arguments for why we're doing well, in the middle of a difficult international situation," she said. Carlos Slim agreed, calling Moody's rating "irrational."

🇲🇽🌎 US SUPREME COURT LIMITS RÍO BRAVO PUMPING — WATER FLOW TO MEXICO AT STAKE

The US Supreme Court approved a historic agreement limiting underground water extraction from the Río Bravo basin, ending New Mexico's unchecked pumping that reduced flow along the Mexico-US border.

The ruling strips irrigation rights from southern New Mexico farming zones and mandates long-term fallowing programs. "We are very enthusiastic about redirecting resources from costly litigation," said Interstate Waterway Commission director Hanna Riseley-White.

The Río Bravo sustains millions across Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas. Scientists warn drought and overexploitation threaten the entire basin — any upstream regulation that protects flow is a direct win for Mexico's water security.
